purpose: Butorphanol is a strong pain reliever used to treat moderate to severe pain, such as after surgery or for migraine headaches. It is also sometimes used before or during medical procedures to help manage pain and anxiety. The nasal spray version is especially helpful for people who need quick relief from severe migraines.
how_it_works: Butorphanol works by attaching to special receptors in your brain and nervous system called opioid receptors. When it attaches to these receptors, it blocks pain signals from reaching your brain, so you feel less pain. It acts a little differently than other opioids because it both activates some receptors and partially blocks others, which is why it is called a mixed agonist-antagonist.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or dizziness, nausea or vomiting, feeling lightheaded, headache, a floating or strange feeling, sweating, dry mouth, and nasal irritation or congestion if you use the nasal spray.
warnings: This medication can cause serious breathing problems, especially if you take too much or combine it with alcohol, sleeping pills, or other opioids — this can be life-threatening. It can be habit-forming, so use it exactly as prescribed. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, as it can harm the baby. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as withdrawal symptoms can occur.
typical_dosing: For the nasal spray, the usual starting dose is one spray (1 mg) in one nostril. If pain is not relieved after 60 to 90 minutes, a second spray may be given. For injection (given in a hospital or clinic), the typical dose is 1 to 2 mg every 3 to 4 hours as needed. Your doctor will adjust the dose based on your individual needs and response.
